key: The multitude of men look satisfied and pleased; as if enjoying a full banquet, as if mounted on a tower in spring. I alone seem listless and still, my desires having as yet given no indication of their presence.
s: The chapter says the multitude look pleased, as if at a full banquet, while ‘I alone’ seem listless and still, desires not yet showing; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 20, reads their pleasure as dissolute desire, like a hungry man craving a feast and never satisfied, and the stillness as calm, with no form or sign of passion yet.

evidence.words: 熙熙，放淫多情欲也。…如飢思太牢之具，意無足時也。…我獨怕然安靜，未有情慾之形兆也。
evidence.gloss: ‘Merry’ means unrestrained, dissolute and full of passions and desires. … Like a hungry man longing for the dishes of a full banquet: the mind has no time of being satisfied. … I alone am placid, calm and still, with as yet no form or sign of passion and desire.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Tao Te Ching 20, at [19]). The Heshang Gong base text 眾人熙熙，如享太牢，如春登臺。我獨怕兮其未兆 matches the key verse; its comments on 熙熙, 如享太牢 and 我獨怕兮其未兆 carry the sentence’s reading (dissolute desire, the hungry man never satisfied, calm stillness with no form or sign of passion) without drift. The comment on 如春登臺 is not used, which is fine. Plain sense restates the key verse. entry-check ok.
